args.body:
REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM
Investment Advisory Agreement — Counterparty Markup Analysis
Funds / Asset Management

TO:      Deal Team / Client
FROM:    Funds & Asset Management Practice
RE:      Comprehensive Redline Review of Counterparty Markup to Investment Advisory Agreement
DATE:    [Engagement Date]
STATUS:  CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

================================================================================
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

This memorandum reviews the counterparty’s redlined investment advisory agreement against the firm’s standard form, the base deal materials for this funds/asset-management engagement, the disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the controlling client instructions in the latest deal-team correspondence.

The counterparty accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations:

  (1) Indemnification economics — silent reduction of the indemnification cap and conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping (first-dollar) basket;
  (2) Material Adverse Effect (MAE) definition — new carve-outs for regulatory action of the type already at issue in this matter; and
  (3) Survival / limitation period — a shortened limitation period that reduces survival for the core representations and contradicts the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Reconciliation against the schedules and exhibits is essential. Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the proposed MAE carve-outs. Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the indemnification changes would silently reallocate. Exhibit B sets the survival matrix that the limitation-period change contradicts. Under the base materials, the scheduled exceptions control over general statements.

Controlling client instruction (latest partner email): the client will concede the basket conversion (deductible → tipping) but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded and are not followed in this memorandum.

Misfiled correspondence from an unrelated engagement that may appear in the matter folder has been disregarded and forms no part of this analysis.

Recommended posture (in priority order consistent with controlling instructions):

  • REJECT and treat as walk-away: any shortening of survival for core representations (Deviation 3).
  • REJECT / require restore: silent indemnification-cap reduction; require express negotiation and disclosure of any cap change (Deviation 1 — cap component).
  • CONCEDE (per client): basket conversion from deductible to tipping basket (Deviation 1 — basket component), subject to clean documentation and no collateral shifts via Schedule 5.2.
  • REJECT / require narrow: MAE regulatory-action carve-outs that would neutralize Schedule 3.7 risk (Deviation 2).

================================================================================
II. SCOPE, MATERIALS REVIEWED, AND METHODOLOGY
================================================================================

A. Engagement Instruction

Review the redlined investment advisory agreement against the standard form and internal playbook, and prepare a comprehensive redline review memorandum (output: redline-review-memorandum.docx). Reconcile the counterparty markup against the base materials and address every deviation.

B. Materials Reviewed (Operative Record Only)

  1. Deal materials — funds-asset-management (Matter File 15): base engagement record, key provisions (representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, termination), open issues, and requested action.
  2. Counterparty markup — funds-asset-management: counterparty revision identifying the three deviations listed above.
  3. Schedules and exhibits — funds-asset-management: Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries); Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities); Exhibit B (survival matrix). Scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials.
  4. Deal correspondence — funds-asset-management: partner email thread; latest message controls analysis priorities (concede basket conversion; survival-period reduction is walk-away).

C. Materials Disregarded

Misfiled correspondence from an unrelated engagement present in the matter folder has not been relied upon. Superseded earlier messages in the deal-team thread (opposite priority ordering) are noted only to confirm they do not control.

D. Methodology

For each counterparty deviation we (i) state the firm-standard / base position, (ii) describe the markup change, (iii) reconcile against schedules/exhibits and the regulatory posture of this matter, (iv) apply the controlling client instruction, and (v) recommend Accept / Reject / Counter with proposed fallback language themes. Playbook posture for investment advisory agreements in this practice area prioritizes: intact survival for core advisory representations (authority, Advisers Act / status, conflicts, fees, AUM/performance calculation integrity); transparent indemnification economics (no silent cap cuts); MAE definitions that do not pre-empt known regulatory exposure; and alignment of disclosure schedules with operative risk allocation.

================================================================================
III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCTION AND BASKET CONVERSION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Base / Standard-Form Position

Firm-standard investment advisory agreement indemnification economics typically provide:

  • A negotiated aggregate indemnification cap (often a stated percentage of advisory fees over a reference period, or a fixed dollar cap tied to deal economics), expressly disclosed in the indemnification article and any related fee/liability schedule.
  • A deductible basket: the indemnified party bears losses until the basket threshold is exceeded, and only amounts above the threshold are recoverable (true deductible), protecting the advisor from nickel-and-dime claims while preserving meaningful recovery once materiality is shown.
  • Express cross-references to Schedule 5.2 (or equivalent) for retained liabilities so that scheduled items are not double-counted or silently shifted by changes to cap/basket mechanics.

B. Counterparty Markup

The counterparty’s revision (i) silently reduces the indemnification cap and (ii) converts the basket from a deductible to a tipping (first-dollar) basket. “Silently” means the cap reduction is effected without prominent redline call-out commensurate with the economic significance of the change and without conforming edits to related schedules and definitions.

C. Reconciliation to Schedules and Base Materials

Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup’s indemnification changes would silently shift. Interaction effects:

  1. Cap reduction + retained liabilities: If Schedule 5.2 items are carved out of the cap or treated as buyer/client-retained, a lower cap on the remaining indemnity pool further compresses recovery for unscheduled breaches (including core advisory representations). Conversely, if Schedule 5.2 items remain inside the indemnified set, a reduced cap may be exhausted by known retained items, leaving inadequate headroom for unknown breaches.
  2. Tipping basket + Schedule 5.2: A tipping basket causes the entire loss stack (from dollar one) to become recoverable once the threshold is crossed. Combined with Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities, this can either (a) accelerate recovery in the client’s favor once the tip is hit, or (b) if the counterparty simultaneously narrows what counts toward the basket or carves scheduled items out of indemnification, produce a net shift of economic risk onto the client despite the “client-friendly” appearance of a tipping basket.
  3. Control rule: Scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials. Any indemnification redline must be read together with Schedule 5.2; the deliverable cannot treat the cap/basket edits in isolation.

D. Controlling Client Instruction

The client will concede the basket conversion (deductible → tipping). The client has not authorized concession of the silent cap reduction. Cap economics remain a live negotiate/reject item.

E. Risk Assessment

  • Silent cap reduction is high risk: it alters the fundamental quantum of post-closing recourse without transparent negotiation and may interact adversely with Schedule 5.2.
  • Basket conversion is moderate risk / client-authorized concession: tipping baskets are often client-favorable once the threshold is met; the principal residual risk is definitional gaming (what counts toward the basket; relationship to scheduled retained liabilities; fraud/willful-breach carve-outs from the basket).

F. Recommendation

  1. CAP COMPONENT — REJECT silent reduction. Require restoration of the firm-standard / base cap, or an expressly negotiated alternative cap with conforming edits to the indemnification article, definitions, and Schedule 5.2 cross-references. Condition any alternative on a clear schedule of what sits inside/outside the cap (including Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities) so there is no silent shift.
  2. BASKET COMPONENT — ACCEPT conversion to tipping basket per controlling client instruction, subject to:
       (a) express drafting that once the basket threshold is exceeded, losses are recoverable from dollar one;
       (b) confirmation that Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities do not create an unintended double materiality or exclusion that nullifies the tip;
       (c) preservation of standard carve-outs from the basket for fraud, willful breach, and fundamental representations (as defined in the base form / Exhibit B survival matrix);
       (d) no collateral narrowing of “Losses” or claim procedures that would claw back the value of the concession.
  3. DOCUMENTATION CLEAN-UP — Require a single conforming set of indemnification definitions so cap, basket, Schedule 5.2, and survival provisions are internally consistent.

G. Proposed Counter-Language Themes (Cap)

  • Restore prior cap quantum and calculation base (e.g., trailing advisory fees / agreed reference amount).
  • Add express schedule mapping: “For the avoidance of doubt, liabilities set forth on Schedule 5.2 shall [count toward / be excluded from] the Cap as specified on Schedule 5.2, and no reduction to the Cap shall be effected except by written amendment that expressly references this Section and Schedule 5.2.”
  • Reject any “deemed” or buried cap reduction via definitions of “Indemnifiable Losses” or similar.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 2 — MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT DEFINITION; REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Base / Standard-Form Position

Firm-standard MAE definitions in investment advisory agreements protect the client’s walk-right / closing condition and bring-down if events materially impair the advisory business, AUM, fee stream, regulatory standing, or ability to perform. Regulatory investigations, enforcement actions, and Advisers Act / status impairments are typically within the MAE concept or are addressed through separate regulatory representations, covenants, and conditions, not broadly carved out of MAE.

B. Counterparty Markup

The definition of Material Adverse Effect adds carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter. The practical effect is to prevent known or foreseeable regulatory developments from constituting (or contributing to) an MAE, thereby weakening the client’s condition to closing and related termination/remedy rights.

C. Reconciliation to Schedules and Base Materials

Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the markup’s MAE carve-outs. Under the control rule, scheduled exceptions qualify the base representations; they do not authorize the counterparty to eliminate MAE coverage for the very risk profile disclosed.

Interaction effects:

  1. If MAE excludes “regulatory action” broadly, escalation or adverse resolution of the two Schedule 3.7 inquiries may be incapable of supporting an MAE claim even if they destroy AUM, fee revenue, or registrability.
  2. Disclosure on Schedule 3.7 may be used by the counterparty to argue both that (i) the matters are known (no MAE because “known matters” or specific regulatory carve-outs apply) and (ii) bring-down of regulatory representations is satisfied because they were scheduled — a double insulation that the base form does not contemplate.
  3. For an investment advisory business, regulatory standing is core to the asset being acquired/engaged; carving it out of MAE is commercially misaligned with funds/asset-management risk allocation and firm playbook.

D. Controlling Client Instruction

No client concession was granted on MAE regulatory carve-outs. Only basket conversion was authorized for concession. Survival remains walk-away; MAE should be defended consistent with preserving meaningful closing conditionality around regulatory risk.

E. Risk Assessment

High. Given Schedule 3.7’s two pending regulatory inquiries, the carve-outs are not theoretical — they target the live risk. Accepting them would largely nullify MAE protection for the principal disclosed contingency in this matter.

F. Recommendation — REJECT / NARROW

  1. Reject broad carve-outs for “regulatory action,” “investigations,” “inquiries,” or similar that would sweep in the Schedule 3.7 matters or Advisers Act / registration impairment.
  2. If a limited known-matters construct is commercially necessary, confine it tightly:
       (a) reference only the specific items disclosed on Schedule 3.7 as they exist on the date of the agreement;
       (b) exclude from the carve-out any material worsening, expansion of scope, enforcement action, penalty, bar, censure, registration impairment, or AUM/fee impact beyond a defined threshold;
       (c) preserve separate regulatory representations, interim operating covenants, and closing conditions (including no material adverse regulatory development) so that MAE is not the sole protective device;
       (d) clarify that scheduling an inquiry is disclosure, not risk transfer, unless expressly agreed in the indemnification and Schedule 5.2 mechanics.
  3. Align MAE with investment-adviser-specific concepts: loss of key personnel only if desired as a separate prong; impairment of registration, exempt status, or ability to collect advisory fees should remain MAE-capable.

G. Proposed Counter-Language Themes (MAE)

  • Delete counterparty regulatory-action carve-outs in full; or
  • Replace with: “excluding the existence (but not any Material Adverse Effect arising from the worsening, expansion, or resolution) of the specific matters set forth on Schedule 3.7 as of the date hereof.”
  • Add express: “For the avoidance of doubt, any Order, enforcement action, or restriction that materially impairs the Company’s registration as an investment adviser, exempt status, or ability to perform the Advisory Services shall not be excluded from Material Adverse Effect by reason of Schedule 3.7.”

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 3 — LIMITATION PERIOD; SHORTENED SURVIVAL FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Base / Standard-Form Position

Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for representations and warranties under the base materials. Core / fundamental representations in an investment advisory agreement context typically include organization/authority, ownership of the advisory contracts and intellectual property necessary to perform, Advisers Act registration and status, conflicts and affiliated-transaction compliance, fee and AUM calculation integrity, and related regulatory standing. Firm playbook and Exhibit B provide longer survival (or survival through the applicable statute of limitations) for fundamental representations, with a standard survival window for business representations and special treatment for tax and certain regulatory items as specified in the matrix.

B. Counterparty Markup

A new limitation period shortens survival for the core representations. This directly contradicts Exhibit B’s survival matrix.

C. Reconciliation to Schedules and Base Materials

  1. Exhibit B controls the survival architecture. A markup that shortens core-rep survival without amending Exhibit B creates an internal conflict; under the instruction that scheduled exceptions (and by parity, the survival exhibit) control over general statements, Exhibit B should prevail unless expressly amended by negotiated agreement.
  2. Shortened survival compounds Deviations 1 and 2: even if indemnification cap/basket and MAE were acceptable, truncated survival on core reps (especially regulatory and fee/AUM integrity) would cut off remedies for the very risks Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2 highlight, often before regulatory proceedings resolve.
  3. Pending regulatory inquiries (Schedule 3.7) frequently outlast abbreviated contractual limitation periods. Accepting a short core-rep survival period would systematically under-protect the client relative to known timelines.

D. Controlling Client Instruction — WALK-AWAY

The latest deal-team correspondence states that the client treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded. This memorandum treats Deviation 3 as non-negotiable rejection territory unless and until the client issues a superseding written instruction.

E. Risk Assessment

Critical / deal-breaking under current instructions. Commercial and regulatory rationale strongly supports the client position: core advisory representations are the backbone of post-closing recourse in funds/asset-management transactions.

F. Recommendation — REJECT (WALK-AWAY)

  1. Reject any shortening of survival for core / fundamental representations.
  2. Require express conformity to Exhibit B’s survival matrix; any agreed modification must be effected by amending Exhibit B in a transparent, bilateral schedule—not by a buried limitation-period clause in the general provisions.
  3. Preserve standard tolling for pending claims and fraud/willful misconduct outside the limitation period.
  4. If the counterparty seeks symmetry or administrative simplicity, counter with tiered survival consistent with Exhibit B rather than a uniform short period that collapses fundamental and ordinary reps.

G. Proposed Counter-Language Themes (Survival)

  • “The representations and warranties of the parties shall survive the Closing for the periods set forth on Exhibit B (Survival Matrix), which Exhibit B is incorporated by reference and shall control over any conflicting limitation period in this Agreement.”
  • “No amendment to survival periods applicable to Fundamental Representations shall be effective unless it expressly amends Exhibit B.”
  • Maintain claim-notice tolling: timely notice within the survival window preserves the claim until final resolution.

================================================================================
IV. CROSS-CUTTING RECONCILIATION (MARKUP × SCHEDULES × EXHIBITS)
================================================================================

The three deviations must be assessed as a package because they interact:

  ┌────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┐
  │ Deviation                  │ Schedule / Exhibit Touchpoint│ Combined Effect if Accepted│
  ├────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
  │ Cap ↓ (silent)             │ Schedule 5.2 retained liabs  │ Exhausts or reallocates    │
  │                            │                              │ indemnity pool; silent     │
  │                            │                              │ economic shift             │
  ├────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
  │ Basket → tipping           │ Schedule 5.2; Loss defs      │ Client-favorable if clean; │
  │ (CONCEDE per client)       │                              │ risk if definitions game   │
  │                            │                              │ the tip or scheduled items │
  ├────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
  │ MAE regulatory carve-outs  │ Schedule 3.7 (2 inquiries)   │ Nullifies MAE for live     │
  │                            │                              │ regulatory risk            │
  ├────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
  │ Shortened core-rep survival│ Exhibit B survival matrix    │ Cuts off remedies before   │
  │ (WALK-AWAY)                │ + Schedule 3.7 timelines     │ regulatory matters resolve │
  └────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┘

Integrated holding: Even the client-authorized basket concession should be documented only in a package that (i) restores or transparently renegotiates the cap with Schedule 5.2 mapping, (ii) rejects or tightly narrows MAE regulatory carve-outs in light of Schedule 3.7, and (iii) fully restores Exhibit B survival for core representations. Accepting basket conversion in isolation while leaving the other deviations in place would not reflect the controlling instruction and would leave the client materially under-protected.

================================================================================
V. OTHER PROVISIONS
================================================================================

The counterparty’s revision accepts most firm-standard provisions outside the three identified deviations. No additional material deviations are identified in the counterparty markup materials. Standard-form provisions regarding representations and warranties (other than survival), covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification procedure (other than cap/basket quantum and type), and termination should be confirmed on the next full turn of the draft for conforming edits and for any cascading definitional changes introduced to implement the three deviations (e.g., redefinitions of “Losses,” “Fundamental Representations,” “Material Adverse Effect,” or “Indemnifying Party”).

Playbook watch-items for the conforming review (not presently flagged as counterparty deviations, but to be verified when cap/basket/MAE/survival are restored):

  • Advisers Act compliance representations and interim covenants remain uncapped or subject to fundamental treatment consistent with Exhibit B.
  • Fee, performance, and AUM calculation representations align with indemnification and audit/access rights.
  • Assignment / change-of-control and key-person provisions remain consistent with fund documents and advisory contracts.
  • Governing law, venue, and dispute resolution unchanged from firm standard unless separately negotiated.
  • No most-favored or stealth limitation on equitable remedies or specific performance for restrictive covenants and confidentiality.

================================================================================
VI. ACCEPT / REJECT / COUNTER SUMMARY TABLE
================================================================================

  Item                                  | Disposition              | Authority / Rationale
  --------------------------------------|--------------------------|----------------------------------
  Indemnification cap reduction (silent)| REJECT / restore or      | No client concession; Schedule
                                        | expressly renegotiate    | 5.2 interaction; playbook
                                        | with Schedule 5.2 map    | transparency requirement
  --------------------------------------|--------------------------|----------------------------------
  Basket: deductible → tipping          | ACCEPT (concede)         | Controlling client instruction
                                        | with clean drafting and  | (latest deal correspondence);
                                        | Schedule 5.2 safeguards  | residual definitional guards
  --------------------------------------|--------------------------|----------------------------------
  MAE — regulatory-action carve-outs    | REJECT / tightly narrow  | Schedule 3.7 two pending
                                        | so Schedule 3.7 risk     | inquiries; regulatory standing
                                        | remains MAE-capable      | core to advisory franchise
  --------------------------------------|--------------------------|----------------------------------
  Limitation period shortening core     | REJECT — WALK-AWAY       | Controlling client instruction;
  representation survival               | Restore Exhibit B matrix | Exhibit B controls; regulatory
                                        |                          | timelines vs. short periods
  --------------------------------------|--------------------------|----------------------------------
  Balance of firm-standard provisions   | ACCEPT (as received)     | Counterparty accepts most
                                        | subject to conforming    | firm-standard provisions
                                        | edit check               |

================================================================================
VII. RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS
================================================================================

  1. Transmit this memorandum to the client for confirmation that survival remains walk-away and that basket conversion remains the sole authorized concession.
  2. Prepare a responsive markup that:
       (a) restores the indemnification cap (or inserts an expressly negotiated alternative with Schedule 5.2 mapping);
       (b) implements the tipping basket with basket-carve-outs for fraud, willful breach, and fundamental representations, and with clear Loss/Schedule 5.2 mechanics;
       (c) deletes or tightly narrows MAE regulatory carve-outs with a Schedule 3.7 “existence vs. worsening” construct;
       (d) restores Exhibit B survival for all core representations and adds an express control clause in favor of Exhibit B.
